$comment: PHASE 106 — the byline for the imported engineering corpus.
THIS IS AN EDITORIAL DESK, NOT A PERSON, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE.
The Journal's ArticleAuthorProfile model is person-shaped: it carries a
headline, a company, a role title, a location and a `verifiedExpert` flag.
Filling those with an invented engineer — a name, an employer, a certification
and a number of years in the field — would be fabricating professional
credentials to make technical content look more authoritative than its
provenance supports. Attributing 150 articles to a real named individual who
did not write them would be the same falsehood with a real person's name on
it.
So the byline is the organisation's own editorial function, and the
person-shaped fields are either the organisation's genuine public facts or
left null:
company        the real registered organisation identity (lib/seo/config.ts)
roleTitle      what this profile IS — an editorial desk
location       omitted; a desk has no personal location to claim
verifiedExpert FALSE. This flag renders an 'expert verified' badge in the
UI and means a human reviewer vouched for an individual's
expertise. Nobody has done that here, so it stays false.
industrialCredibilityScore  null — a computed reputation signal, not a
value to hand-set.
`userId` is a sentinel, not a cuid, so it can never collide with a real
user account and no signed-in user can inherit this profile through the
submit route's findUnique({ where: { userId } }) lookup.
headline: Industrial automation, electrical engineering and OT systems — the Hermes editorial desk
bio: The Hermes engineering editorial desk publishes reference material on industrial automation, electrical power, control systems, industrial networks and operational technology. Articles are written for practising engineers and describe engineering method: architecture decisions and their consequences, failure mechanisms, evidence-based diagnostics, commissioning practice and lifecycle considerations. Industrial scenarios are presented as illustrative engineering examples unless a source is explicitly cited; they are not accounts of named customer projects. Standards are referenced at the level of their scope and intent rather than by quoting clause numbers.
